content: Since it is in the present and only in the present that you live, there is no other reality than present reality.
author: Alan Watts
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. Holding onto anger is like clutching a glowing coal with the intent of throwing it at someone else—you are the one who gets burned. Retaliation only ties you tighter to the person who harmed you.

Alan Watts understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. Forgiveness and composure are not signs of weakness or giving someone a pass. They are acts of fierce self-preservation, cutting the emotional chain that allows another person's bad behavior to ruin your peace of mind.
reflectionPrompt: How does adopting this philosophical view alter the way you handle current friction?

practicalInsight: When someone triggers your temper today, take three slow breaths before responding. Do not give away your power for the sake of a quick comeback.
